subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should a durable wake resolved before `/new`, `/reset`, or daily/idle rollover be discarded with the old session generation, or intentionally transferred into the new conversation sharing that sessionKey?
rationale: Current documentation and sibling queue behavior preserve session-generation isolation, but this new durable feature could deliberately define a different cross-reset contract only with explicit maintainer intent and matching user-visible documentation.

options.title: Fence to resolved generation
options.body: Persist the resolved sessionId as expectedSessionId and skip mismatched queue entries after rollover, preserving the current reset boundary.

options.title: Carry wakes across reset
options.body: Explicitly approve transfer into the current generation, then document and test that durable obligations survive user and automatic resets.

options.title: Pause the cumulative stack
options.body: Keep the stack unmerged until durable runtime ownership, release scope, and reset semantics are sponsored as one product direction.

recommendation.title: Fence to resolved generation
recommendation.body: Persist the resolved sessionId as expectedSessionId and skip mismatched queue entries after rollover, preserving the current reset boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work most directly covers restart continuation identity, stale handoff state, and session continuity.
